fatal_errors: The proposed Zr-based alloy and boron addition are unrelated to the target Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 alloy and its Fe/Co/Mn/P compositional adjustment.
It predicts a broader supercooled-liquid region and higher glass-transition temperature, whereas the target study detected no glass transition.
No evidence supports the claimed beneficial 1–5 at.% boron range or even identifies a specific baseline Zr alloy.
It omits the decisive processing boundary: full amorphization occurred only in approximately 20 μm ribbons melt-spun at 40 m/s, while the slower-cooled ingot crystallized.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses glass-forming ability only at a generic level and offers a reasonable controlled DSC/XRD falsification experiment. However, it does not reconstruct the material, compositional intervention, processing conditions, eutectic/phosphide mechanism, or measured outcomes of the target study. Its boron-based mechanism is speculative because no specific Zr composition or supporting evidence is supplied. The target enhancement arose from adjusting Fe/Co/Mn ratios and lowering P to 15 at.%, which promoted eutectic-dominated solidification; rapid melt spinning then suppressed segregation and phosphide nucleation to produce an amorphous ribbon.
